item.title: Understanding 'Since' on Nervos CKB (1 posts)
item.description: What it solves, how it works, and how to integrate it into a CKB application Imagine building an application on Nervos CKB where a user deposits an asset today but should not be able to spend it until a future date. The same requirement might arise in token vesting, a treasury release, or a payment-channel dispute period. The Cell exists, and someone may already be authorized to spend it. The missing piece is time: the transaction should not be valid yet. CKB addresses this need through `since`, a small transaction-input field with an important purpose: expressing when an input is eligible to be committed. Once you understand that role, since becomes useful well beyond a simple timelock....

item.title: Ckb-connect-wallet-kit is on npm: compound React wallet UI for CCC, now with did:ckb (1 posts)
item.description: Hi everyone, Back in April I posted a revamp of the CKB wallet connection UI as a compound React component on top of CCC. The feedback from CKB builders was consistent: this should be installable as a package, not something you copy out of a demo. That package is now live as ckb-connect-wallet-kit. You wrap your own ccc.Provider, compose the button / icon / balance / address yourself, and optionally show the connected lock’s did:ckb avatar, display name, and identifier. The kit never mounts CCC. Current version is 0.2.1. item.title: Asset Price Oracle on Nervos Network (1 posts)
item.description: Thanks for the very explicit design write-up, and for stating the limits plainly. One question on price_feed_type: the update rule is new.publish_time_ms > old.publish_time_ms. Is there also an upper bound on publish_time_ms relative to the transaction, for example against a header dep timestamp plus a small skew? If not, a single quorum-signed tick with a timestamp far in the future, from a publisher clock bug or a bad leader proposal that signers do not reject, would make every later honest update fail the strictly-newer check and freeze that feed cell until the committee is replaced and consumers re-pin. item.title: Routed Machine Payment Sessions on Fiber — Looking for Community Feedback (1 posts)
item.description: Thanks for asking before building. One design question on createPaymentSession({ budget }): where is the budget enforced? If it is a counter inside the SDK, the agent process (or a prompt-injected tool call) can bypass or reset it, so the cap is only as strong as that process. A harder bound is to make the budget the funded amount itself: one dedicated channel per session, funded with exactly `budget`, so the worst-case loss is the funding rather than the policy code. Related: with several providers paid in parallel, which component decides that two concurrent requests would together exceed the remaining budget, and if the counter cannot be read, does it deny or allow?
